domain: Energy / Grid Operations (SCADA setpoint configuration governance)
app_concept: Helios Grid Console — a regional transmission operator's control-room workspace where every managed asset's setpoint is stored as a stack of override layers, a governance policy decides which layer wins, and a commissioning standard states what a conforming audit must produce.
modalities: A generated export — the checklist exists only after the conformance matrix is rendered, and is read from that document rather than from the page that offers it.
A settings-style record read as text, then a ranked figure opened from it — the layer sequence is legible as rank positions in the authority panel rather than as a printed list on the policy page.

A standards viewer: front matter read as text, then each normative part opened from it in turn — a clause body, a conditions-of-use section held separate from it, and an annex published as an appendix to the clause body and reachable only once that body has been opened.

Filtering and paging a roster to enumerate the population, then drilling into a record and expanding a section that starts collapsed. The ledger's rendering is load-bearing: absence of a layer, a declared entry with no value, and a declared entry with a zero-length value must each be readable as themselves rather than inferred from a shared placeholder.

provenance: This is capture-analysis data and belongs to the packet-capture indexing and network-forensics category — the Arkime/Moloch, CloudShark, Wireshark, ExtraHop family, together with the trace-replay tooling (tcpreplay-style) those consoles wrap. What led there: the top-level unit is a session keyed by session_id whose protocol is drawn from tcp|udp; each session carries an array of frames, and a frame carries a monotonic tick, a message_id, a fragment_index against a fragment_count, and a payload_hex that is lowercase and even-length — i.e. a byte dump. Fragment index/count with a whole-message drop when any fragment is absent is stream reassembly, and an ordering that dispatches by tick then by a fixed protocol priority is a replay scheduler draining a capture. Sessions, frames, reassembly and byte panes are the vocabulary of a capture console; nothing here reads as a message broker, a job queue or an issue tracker. The policy object is a saved reassembly/replay profile of exactly the kind those consoles keep in a profile library, and the contract and edge-case checklist are the replay engine's format reference and regression suite.
app_concept: Kestrel Capture Console — an offline packet-capture analysis workspace for stored capture sets: sessions are found with a display-filter query, a session's frames are inspected one at a time down to their bytes, deterministic trace replay runs from a saved reassembly profile, and the replay engine ships its own output-format reference and regression suite.
modalities: A display-filter query whose result set does not exist until it is submitted, then master–detail selection twice over: a session's frames exist only once that session is open, and a frame's bytes exist only while the inspector is bound to that frame. The query's scope is load-bearing — the console opens scoped to the most recently rotated capture segment, which holds only part of the stored sessions, so the scope has to be widened to the whole capture set before the result set is the whole population.

A record that has to be located before it can be read: the profile library opens ordered by last-modified, an ordering under which the in-force profile is not on the listing, so it is reached by re-sorting the library by status or by narrowing it by name — and its parameters exist only on its own detail surface, never as library columns.

A sequential document with no jump-to index — the reference is advanced a page at a time and each page has to be passed through to reach the next, so the contract is read in order rather than opened part by part from a contents list.

Content filed by kind behind two mutually exclusive views of one suite — each kind read whole once selected, and the suite returned to before the other kind can be opened. The case pinned to the empty capture is deliberately incomplete here: it names the reference's baseline page as its expectation rather than reprinting it, so the concrete baseline keeps a single home.

provenance: This is an enterprise content management system's document library and upload console — the family of SharePoint document libraries, Box, Egnyte, M-Files, Alfresco and OpenText Content Server — together with the integration developer portal such platforms ship. What led there: each record is one stored document carrying an opaque document identifier, a file name, a byte size that may be unreported, an internet media type, a display label distinct from the file name, an ingestion state drawn from a ready/uploading/failed set, and a flag saying whether it is staged for the next upload. That is a document-library row plus a transfer, not a business entity. The policy object reinforces it: an allowlist of accepted media types, a maximum file-name length, a rows-per-page size, a size-unit base of 1024, a set of transfer states, a keyboard key that submits an upload, and a set of preview viewport widths — this is exactly the administration surface of a document library, not application domain configuration. The contract then describes list rows carrying accessible labels, a size string with a fallback for unreported sizes, a priority-ordered upload hint, a per-row checkbox that toggles selection, and an upload dialog submitted by form or by keyboard — i.e. the published behaviour contract for a document library's list view and batch-upload modal.
app_concept: Foliant Content Library — an enterprise ECM workspace where a shared library of documents is browsed page by page, each item's technical metadata sits on its properties surface, in-flight ingestion is watched from a transfer monitor, the set staged for the next upload sits in the upload console, library behaviour is administered from settings, and the view-model an integrator must reproduce is published in a developer center with a runnable sample-request console.
modalities: A batch-upload dialog holding the staged set in the order items were added to it, collected in one visit and joined back to the listing by identifier. Its order is neither the library's nor the contract's, so the staged-identifier ordering the contract requires must be derived.
A binding read from a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay opened from the top bar, among invented bindings that are chrome. Not reachable from administration or from the library.
A developer portal landing page, read on the way in to every section and the only place the run conditions are stated.

A fourth reference section of the same portal, opened separately from the landing page; it is the only surface that ties an event to a key, and it names the layout descriptor as the home of the narrow breakpoint and library administration as the home of the widths.

A paged listing ordered by an invented operational column, walked page by page to enumerate the population. The active sort is never the ordering the contract requires, so the name-then-identifier order has to be derived from the collected rows rather than read off the screen.

A per-row drill from the listing into a properties surface that holds one element at a time, so the surface is reached once per element and left again before the next can be opened. The rendering of the byte count is load-bearing: an element whose size is recorded as zero and an element whose size was never reported must each read as themselves, since collapsing them into a shared placeholder destroys both the fallback text and the accessible label the contract demands.
A reference section opened in its own right from the developer landing page and left again by its own return before another can be opened.

A request console reached only from the endpoint reference, where this outcome does not exist as printed text: it has to be produced by composing a call over an empty document set and executing it, then read from the returned response body.
A second reference section of the same portal, opened separately from the landing page; nothing in the endpoint reference leads to it.
A second tab of the same administration screen, reached only by switching tabs from the general one.
A set of values legible only as the options a toolbar control offers, never written out as a setting. Not reachable from administration.
A side surface of the same application — an ingestion queue listing every tracked transfer, collected in one visit and joined back to the listing by identifier.
A tabbed administration screen read as text.
A third reference section of the same portal, opened separately from the landing page.
The product's own built-in document previewer: a stored document opened from a collection and read page by page, which is the one modality an enterprise document library is fundamentally about.
